dimensions.note: The SSH private key is sensitive-marked on the string and its nullish wrapper; the canonical vendored _lib/ssh.ts (blob 8f132c43, reviewed in ssh-host 2026.10.17.3) loads it into a short-lived per-call ssh-agent over stdin, so no key text, key path or -i option reaches argv or disk (live cell e: ps scan clean, IdentityFile=none, IdentityAgent per call). The ControlMaster/multiplex path and the in-memory inline-key nonce map are gone. The S3 accessKey/secretKey are sensitive and used only to sign SigV4; RGW user keys and CSI client keys go into sensitive, vaulted resource fields. Known external issue swamp-club lab 3555: README examples pass secrets as vault references only and never show --json. No secret-like literals in the 2026.10.17.3 history (fixtures RFC 5737, placeholder password, sha256('abc') vector).
Methods log structured, value-free summaries (host, method, verdict); remote stderr and S3 transport detail are URL-stripped and truncated before they reach logs or errors.

Failures are typed (validate, transport, unverifiable, protected, object-leak-*, policy rollback) with bounded detail. Under the canonical transport every ssh exit 255 is a typed transport error; every canonical SshError except its typed timeout maps to an outcome-unknown TransportError (never classified from message text), so a mid-session reset or auth failure is never re-sent (tests assert exactly one ssh spawn). A call without budgetMs keeps the 30s budget + 5s grace. Over-cap stdout throws (the canonical truncate option is never passed). cephDeleteFs fails closed unless the client count is a non-negative integer; cephRemoveOsds refuses unless health is OK or WARN. Residual LOW: toTransportError reads .message from non-Error throws.

602 unit/contract tests with an injected canonical CommandRunner (no socket), including the wipe guard refusal matrix (guard r9 signed off, protected_devices.ts blob 62743884 unchanged), SigV4 known-answer tests, workflow catalog tests (succeeded-only edges; every step input key checked against its method's strict schema) and plain-object method contexts, including a model test that runs a method twice under insecure_tofu and asserts learn-then-reuse of the persisted pin. The transport swap was checked with a harness: 3200 distinct remote commands and stdin bodies byte-identical to the pre-swap code. Live at a792f41 on a bare-metal host: 12/13 pass plus 1 observation (guard and wipe cells G1-G6 on scsi_debug RAM disks with OS disks dry-run, strict and wrong-pin refusal, insecure_tofu persists and reuses the pin, a bare host-key line refused, the legacy strictHostKeyChecking input refused naming host_key_policy, ps scan clean); the observation (strict without host_keys uses the persisted pin) is intended and documented. Every cluster cell stays BLOCKED (needs three or more hosts with free whole disks), which is why the channel is beta.

Every ensure/apply method reads first and converges or does nothing (bootstrap no-ops on an existing cluster, placement converges to an explicit list keeping quorum, pools/fs/users adopt); delete paths are double-confirmed and re-runs are clean no-ops; maintenance enter/exit prove their effect. Residual LOW: probe-cleanup fallback after an unreadable version listing reports success after a plain DELETE. wipeDiskToRaw reports alreadyRaw only for a zero sector 0 with no table signature and an empty wipefs; otherwise it wipes and zeroes sector 0. Under insecure_tofu the first-seen key is persisted per host:port only after the first authenticated command runs (persisted is set only after the write succeeds) and reused as the pin on later runs; strict uses supplied pins first, then a persisted pin, and refuses with neither.

Public cephadm/ceph CLI over SSH (pinned cephadm binary from a caller-supplied URL), Ceph RGW admin via radosgw-admin, and the RGW S3 API with SigV4; PutObjectAcl (not a second PutObject) for the leak probe; versioning is the three-state model.

One SSH process per call under the canonical transport, with a per-call ssh-agent and temp known_hosts torn down after it; no ControlMaster. Remote temp files are removed in finally paths; S3 responses are capped at 1 MiB; every wait is bounded, and an SSH call without an explicit budget gets the 35s default.

Manifest @randybias/cephadm, two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt (LOGBOOK not packaged). Destructive methods lead with DESTRUCTIVE., read-only with READ-ONLY.; README method table regenerated from source (50 methods, 22 workflows). Fixtures are synthetic (RFC 5737, example.com/.test); leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass. Clean-room provenance is logged in docs/CLEANROOM.md. README documents the transport, the host-key policies and the persisted-pin behaviour.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject; every method argument object is strict with grammars and bounds. host_key_policy is a required strict|insecure_tofu enum and host_keys an optional bounded array of ssh-keyscan lines that must each name their host (a bare type-blob line is refused, so one host's key cannot pass for another's); keyPath and privateKey together are refused; workflow host_keys inputs carry maxItems 64; the persisted hostkeys resource schema is bounded. Residual MEDIUM: the stored hostkeys record is cast, not re-validated, on read. Bucket policy documents are parsed, validated and re-serialized from the validated structure.
34 result resources lifetime infinite with garbageCollection 10; the CSI key resource keeps 2 versions; the hostkeys resource holds one record per host:port.

Host prep, bootstrap, enrol, mon/mgr/mds/osd placement, pools, CephFS, CSI users and keys, maintenance, teardown, RGW users and buckets, plus verify methods for each; every mutator is kind action (25 methods), so no verb tombstones the definition; 22 workflows gate every mutation behind a pre-check and manual approval.

wipeDiskToRaw refuses any device that backs the running or bootable system (protected-device closure over lsblk, blkid, mdstat, mdadm --examine, pvs and ZFS; BIOS-boot/ESP partitions, EFI evidence and MBR boot code in sector 0 of every disk behind a candidate, including multipath, md, LVM and crypt stacks) unless that disk's own serial is acknowledged, and refuses when lsblk and blkid disagree; destructive teardown requires the named fsid; placement changes are judged against live quorum first. Every destructive method enforces its own precondition in-method (guard, health, in-use, joint ok-to-stop, fsid), and every destructive workflow re-gates after approval (swamp lab 3583). Residual MEDIUM: a non-ESP-typed, unmounted EFI boot partition is unprotected on an EFI host where efibootmgr is missing or fails. LOW L-9b: a dm device on a partition of a boot-code disk is refused and cannot be acknowledged (fail-closed).
Workflows address the instance cephadm or cephadm-<purpose>-<item> for a fan-out, and each assert reads the record from the instance that wrote it.
Every host, credential and target arrives as method arguments, so one generic definition serves any cluster; the model reads no other model's data.

2026.10.17.3 adds an identity upgrade entry: strictHostKeyChecking/multiplex were method inputs, never stored attributes, so nothing stored changes. The breaking method-input rename (strictHostKeyChecking -> host_key_policy + host_keys, multiplex dropped) is stated in the release note, README and LOGBOOK; the bundled workflows pass the new inputs and a caller passing the legacy input gets an error listing host_key_policy (live cell d). The chain 2026.10.17.1 -> .2 -> .3 is spelled out on the model export, with a test keeping it equal to the factory's chain. Residual LOW: the migration description duplicates MODEL_UPGRADES.
